Good breakdown. The sequencer FIFO model is exactly why traditional sandwich detection was misleading for my situation. I was looking for mempool-based attacks that do not exist on Arbitrum in the same form.

The real culprit was simpler than MEV: my strategy had a 42% win rate on fast exits because the confidence calibration was broken. High-confidence signals (0.8+) had a 27% win rate. Appreciate all the detailed responses on this thread. A few things I want to address:

First, to clarify: my 122 trades were not 0 percent win rate overall. The 0 percent was specifically the 16 sub-60-second exits. The overall win rate was 39 percent. The fast exits were likely a combination of bad signal timing and yes, possibly some latency-based extraction.
